statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks judged on the parts-catalogue page, its search, pagination and add-to-cart flows, and the targets of its header navigation. The page is served by a static Python http.server fixture (HTTP/1.0, directory listing at /), so server-side behaviour (GET /search, GET/POST /cart, response headers) reflects this host, not necessarily a production deployment.

page.framework: none (static HTML + one shared stylesheet, zero scripts)
page.notes: Product listing page titled 'Parts catalogue'. It has 51 DOM elements, 0 scripts, 0 inline handlers, 0 images and one stylesheet (../base.css, 3 KB) shared with sibling fixture designs. Contents: a header nav (Catalogue -> '/', marked aria-current=page; Cart -> /cart), h1, a GET search form (#search-form -> /search), a 'Results' section with three product cards (h3 name, description, availability; no price, no part number, no link, no button), a pagination nav (1/2/3 -> /search?page=N), and an aside 'Your cart' holding a POST form (#cart-form -> /cart) that asks for a free-text 'Part number' and a quantity. The footer says 'Catalogue prices include VAT.' Every onward route fails on this host: /search and /search?page=N -> 404, /cart -> 404 (GET) and 501 (POST), and '/' is a raw directory listing. Sibling directories (account-recovery/, booking/, contact-lead/, event-registration/) are separate designs, are not linked from this page, and are out of scope; booking/ and account-recovery/ were audited in earlier runs.

evidenceUsed: screenshot (default 780px, full page, 1280x900 full page, 360x800, prefers-color-scheme: dark, forced-colors: active + prefers-contrast: more; destination pages /search?q=bearing and /)

evaluate-probe (form fields + constraint validation, heading outline, links + aria-current, product-card contents, grid placement of main's children, GET/POST of /, /cart, /search, /search?q=, /search?page=2, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, a guessed product URL and a 404 URL; document metadata, protocol, memory)

a11ytree (computed AX tree + real Tab order)
discoverability (raw vs rendered, crawler screenshot pair)
heap summaries (baseline and after 10x fill/validate/clear of both forms)

Flow/form/document probe: field attributes (no required anywhere; quantity min=1, no default), forms valid when empty, heading outline h1 > h3 x3 > h2, aria-current on '/' and on /search?page=1, product cards with no link/button/price/part number, grid placement of main's children, and route results: / directory listing; /cart 404; /search, /search?q=bearing, /search?page=2 404; POST /cart 501; robots.txt, sitemap.xml 404; doctype/charset/http/1.0/0 scripts.
Render under ar-EG / Asia/Tokyo: text identical to default, lang=en, ltr, 0 time elements; the only digits are product sizes (12mm, 15mm) and page numbers.

findings.summary: Every onward journey from the catalogue dead-ends. Searching lands on a 404, all three pagination links 404, the 'Cart' link 404s, 'Add to cart' returns 501 'Unsupported method', and 'Catalogue' opens a raw server directory listing. A shopper can view three cards and nothing else.
findings.evidence: flow-probe: GET /search?q=bearing -> 404, GET /search -> 404, GET /search?page=2 -> 404, GET /cart -> 404, POST /cart (item=Bearing 12mm, quantity=1) -> 501 'Unsupported method (POST)', GET / -> 200 'Directory listing for /'. after-search.png shows the raw 'Error response 404' page a search produces; catalogue-nav-target.png shows the directory listing. Product cards contain no links, so there is no detail page either (a guessed /catalogue/bearing-12mm -> 404). The host is a static fixture, but this is what a user of this deployment gets.
findings.suggestedFix: Back every action the page advertises: a GET /search handler that renders results (and the same template for ?page=N), a GET /cart page, and a POST /cart handler using POST-redirect-GET back to the catalogue (or to the cart) with a confirmation. Point 'Catalogue' at /catalogue/ rather than '/'. If search is not ready, remove the form instead of shipping a dead control.

findings.summary: To add a part, the user must type a 'Part number' that the page never shows. The product cards have no part number, no 'Add' button and no link, so the only cart path asks for hidden required information and invites guesses such as the product name.
findings.evidence: flow-probe articles: all 3 cards have hasPartNumber=false, hasButton=false and hasLink=false (text is name, description and availability only). The only add path is #cart-form, with a free-text #item labelled 'Part number' (type=text, no pattern, no hint, no datalist) and #quantity. The 1280 full-page screenshot shows the cart form in a separate card, away from the products.
findings.suggestedFix: Put the action on the product: give each <article> its own <form method="post" action="/cart"> with <input type="hidden" name="item" value="BRG-12">, a labelled quantity (value="1" min="1") and a 'Add Bearing 12mm to cart' button (visible text 'Add to cart' plus a visually hidden product name). Show the part number on the card. If quick-entry by part number stays, add a hint with the format and a <datalist> of valid numbers.

findings.summary: No prices appear anywhere, yet the footer says 'Catalogue prices include VAT.' Shoppers are asked to add items to a cart without knowing what they cost.
findings.evidence: flow-probe: hasPrice=false on all 3 product cards; the rendered text contains no currency symbol or amount. The footer copy reads 'Catalogue prices include VAT.' (dom.json, desktop-1280-full.png). The Add to cart form shows no unit price or line total either.
findings.suggestedFix:
Show the VAT-inclusive unit price on every card, e.g.

£4.50 inc. VAT, pack of two

, formatted with Intl.NumberFormat or server-side locale formatting. For 'Ordered on request' items, say so explicitly ('Price on request') rather than leaving the price blank.

findings.summary: The layout demotes the products. The 2fr main column holds only the search card while the results are squeezed into the 1fr sidebar column. The pagination lands in the left column below search, detached from the results it pages, leaving a large empty area beside the cards.
findings.evidence: flow-probe mainKids at the 780px capture: form#search-form x=16 w=483 h=150, section[Results] x=523 w=241 h=475, nav[Pagination] x=16 y=641 w=483, aside x=523 y=641 w=241. main uses grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr, and its five children auto-place into alternating columns. desktop-1280-full.png shows the cards in a single narrow column on the right, an empty block under the search card, and '1 2 3' stranded on the left. The auto-fill card grid (minmax(14rem,1fr)) can only fit one card per row in that column.
findings.suggestedFix: Place the regions explicitly: e.g. main { grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr; grid-template-areas: 'h1 h1' 'search cart' 'results cart' 'pages cart'; }, with #search-form { grid-area: search } and so on, or put the search form, results and pagination in one wrapper in the main column and the aside in the sidebar. The results grid then gets the wide column (2-3 cards per row) and the pagination sits directly under the results.

findings.summary: When a route fails, the user gets the bare server error page ('Error response / Error code: 404' or '501 Unsupported method') with no site header, no navigation, no explanation and no way back other than the browser Back button. The search term and cart entry are lost.
findings.evidence: after-search.png: an unstyled 'Error response' page with error code, message and explanation only. flow-probe bodySample is identical for /cart, /search, /search?page=2, /robots.txt and /no-such-page-xyz (404), and POST /cart returns the same template with 501. None carry links back into the catalogue.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve branded error documents that keep the site header and nav. A 404 should say what was not found, link to the catalogue and offer the search box pre-filled with the query. A failed POST /cart should re-render the catalogue with the entered part number and quantity preserved and a role=alert message ('We couldn't add that to your cart. Try again.').

findings.summary: The 'Your cart' panel shows no cart state: no items, no count and no 'Your cart is empty' message, only an entry form. The page has no success or confirmation pattern for an add, so a user cannot tell what is already in the cart.
findings.evidence: dom.json/flow-probe: the aside contains only h2 'Your cart' and #cart-form; liveRegions=0 and there are no role=status/alert elements. desktop-1280-full.png shows the panel with two empty inputs and a button.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the cart summary server-side in the aside (line items, count and subtotal, or 'Your cart is empty'), and after a successful POST-redirect-GET show a role=status confirmation ('Added 2 x Bearing 12mm. View cart').

findings.summary: aria-current="page" is attached to links that are not this page. 'Catalogue' (current) points to '/', a directory listing, and pagination '1' (current) points to /search?page=1. Assistive tech and sighted users are told the current location lives at URLs that are not the one they are on.
findings.evidence: flow-probe links: {text:'Catalogue', href:'http://127.0.0.1:8765/', current:'page'} and {text:'1', href:'http://127.0.0.1:8765/search?page=1', current:'page'} while location is /catalogue/. The a11ytree exposes both links with the current-page state; base.css renders the nav one at font-weight 600. GET / -> 'Directory listing for /'.
findings.suggestedFix: Point 'Catalogue' at /catalogue/ (the page that actually carries aria-current). Render the current pagination item as the current URL (/catalogue/ or /catalogue/?page=1) and make page links share this page's path rather than /search.

findings.summary: The heading outline skips a level: the product names are h3 directly under the h1, and the 'Results' region has no heading of its own, so heading navigation jumps from 'Parts catalogue' to the first product.
findings.evidence: axe heading-order (moderate) on 'article:nth-child(1) > h3'. flow-probe headings: H1 Parts catalogue, H3 Bearing 12mm, H3 Bearing 15mm, H3 Bushing 12mm, H2 Your cart. The section is labelled only by aria-label="Results".
findings.suggestedFix: Give the results section a visible h2 ('Results' or '3 parts') referenced by aria-labelledby, so the product h3s nest correctly. Alternatively make the product names h2.

findings.summary: The add-to-cart form does not prevent obvious mistakes. Neither field is required, so an empty submit goes straight to the server. Quantity has no default. There is no visible invalid state, inline message or hint, so the only feedback is the browser's transient bubble for a quantity below 1.
findings.evidence: flow-probe: #item and #quantity both required=false; #cart-form checkValidity() on an empty form -> true (submittable empty); #quantity min=1 with no value. The features census shows no :user-invalid or :user-valid rule; liveRegions=0; no field has aria-describedby. Per MWG required-field-feedback and forms, required fields should be marked and invalid fields signalled with :user-invalid plus text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add required to both fields (and mark them in the label), give quantity value="1", add a part-number pattern plus a hint linked by aria-describedby, and style input:user-invalid with a border change plus an adjacent message (input:user-invalid + .error-msg { display: block }). On server rejection, re-render with input kept and a role=alert summary.

findings.summary: The identifier inputs leave text correction on. 'Part number' and the search box lack autocorrect="off", autocapitalize="off" and spellcheck="false", so mobile keyboards may 'correct' or capitalise codes. Neither field sets an enterkeyhint.
findings.evidence: flow-probe fields: #item (type=text, label 'Part number') and #q (type=search) both have autocorrect=null, autocapitalize=null, spellcheck=null and no enterkeyhint. MWG forms section 3: 'DO turn off text correction on fields that hold identifiers ... codes, and search inputs.' #quantity correctly uses type=number with min=1.
findings.suggestedFix: <input id="item" name="item" autocomplete="off" autocorrect="off" autocapitalize="characters" spellcheck="false" enterkeyhint="next"> (use autocapitalize="characters" if part numbers are upper-case codes), and add autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" enterkeyhint="search" to #q.

findings.summary: There is no dark mode. The page ignores prefers-color-scheme and does not declare color-scheme, so the light #f4f5f8/#fff surfaces and light form controls stay the same for users who ask for dark.
findings.evidence: dark.png under prefers-color-scheme: dark is byte-identical in size (37,464 B) and visually identical to desktop.png. The features census (complete, 1 sheet) shows color-scheme 0, light-dark() 0 and no prefers-color-scheme condition; the only @media is (max-width: 44rem). flow-probe: no <meta name=color-scheme>.
findings.suggestedFix: In base.css add :root { color-scheme: light dark; } and a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) override of the tokens (--ink, --muted, --line, --paper, --wash, --accent), optionally expressed with light-dark(). Add <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">, then re-check contrast in both schemes (MWG dark-mode).

findings.summary: In forced-colours mode the buttons lose their boundary. They are styled with a background colour and border: 0, so once the system palette replaces the background, 'Search' and 'Add to cart' render as bare bold text with no visible control edge.
findings.evidence: forced-colors.png (forced-colors: active + prefers-contrast: more): the search input and cards keep system-colour borders, but the 'Search' button shows no outline or fill. base.css: 'button { background: var(--accent); ... border: 0px; }'.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a transparent border instead of none: button { border: 2px solid transparent; }. Forced colours then paints it as ButtonText. Alternatively add @media (forced-colors: active) { button { border: 1px solid ButtonText; } } (MWG color: Forced Colors Mode).

findings.summary: body sets font: 16px/1.5, a fixed pixel size that overrides the user's browser or OS default text size. People who raise their default size get no larger body text, card copy or form fields (page zoom still works).
findings.evidence: dom css: 'body { font: 16px / 1.5 system-ui, ... }'. Headings use rem, but card text, labels and the inputs/buttons (font: inherit) stay pinned at 16px; flow-probe bodyFont 16px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a relative size: body { font: 100%/1.5 system-ui, ... } (or 1rem), so text and inherited controls scale with the user's text-size preference (MWG respect-os-text-scale).

findings.summary: Browsing the catalogue (search, page 1 -> 2 -> 3, add to cart -> cart) is a sequence of full-page navigations that swap instantly, with no cross-document view-transition opt-in to keep orientation between result pages.
findings.evidence: features census (complete): @view-transition 0 and view-transition-name 0. There are 0 scripts, so there is no same-document transition either.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } } to base.css, optionally naming the results grid (view-transition-name: results) so paging cross-fades in place. This is pure progressive enhancement; unsupported browsers navigate normally (MWG cross-document-transitions).

findings.summary: The page and its state-changing cart form are served and posted over plain HTTP with no Content-Security-Policy and no X-Content-Type-Options. The POST /cart form carries no anti-CSRF token.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: https=false; content-security-policy and x-content-type-options missing. flow-probe: nextHopProtocol http/1.0; #cart-form method=post action=http://127.0.0.1:8765/cart with only item and quantity fields (no hidden token). 0 cookies at load. Confidence is medium: loopback counts as a secure context (isSecureContext=true), and the fixture host may not reflect production.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve only over HTTPS. Send an enforced Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script', plus X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The page has no scripts, so a strict policy costs nothing. Add a per-session anti-CSRF token to the cart form, and when a cart session cookie is introduced use __Host- with Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (MWG security, forms section 8).

findings.summary: No browser-enforced defences are configured: no HSTS, no clickjacking protection (neither frame-ancestors nor X-Frame-Options), no Referrer-Policy and no Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: strict-transport-security, x-frame-options, referrer-policy and permissions-policy all missing, and there is no CSP to carry frame-ancestors. Lower stakes than a credential page, but the cart form is a state-changing control that could be framed.
findings.suggestedFix: Once on HTTPS, send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, CSP frame-ancestors 'self', Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() (MWG security, privacy).

findings.summary: The only render-blocking resource, base.css, is served uncompressed with no Cache-Control or validators over HTTP/1.0, so every catalogue page view re-downloads it.
findings.evidence: har-summary hygiene: base.css is listed in missingCacheHeaders and uncompressedTextOver2KB (3179 B, content-encoding none). renderBlockingCandidates: base.css (parser-inserted, VeryHigh), confirmed in the DOM as a <link rel=stylesheet> in <head>. flow-probe: nextHopProtocol http/1.0. The absolute cost is small (5.4 KB total) and the throttled LCP is still 529ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve static assets with br/gzip, a versioned filename and Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3. Optionally inline the 3 KB of critical CSS.

findings.summary: The <title> 'Parts catalogue' carries no site or brand name, and there is no meta description, so search results and tabs cannot tell this catalogue apart from any other.
findings.evidence: flow-probe: title 'Parts catalogue', metaDescription=null. discoverability: metaDescriptionPresentInRaw=null (absent).
findings.suggestedFix: <title>Parts catalogue: bearings and bushings - <Site name></title> and <meta name="description" content="Browse sealed bearings and bronze bushings, check stock and order online. Prices include VAT.">. Modern Web Guidance has no SEO guide; this is the Lighthouse SEO bar.

findings.summary: The listing's indexing signals are inconsistent. Page 1 of the pagination is a different URL (/search?page=1) from the page being viewed, there is no rel=canonical to reconcile them, and the catalogue publishes no robots.txt or sitemap to expose its product pages.
findings.evidence: flow-probe: pagination '1' href /search?page=1 with aria-current=page while location is /catalogue/; canonical=null; robots.txt and sitemap.xml -> 404; the paginated URLs themselves -> 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one URL scheme for the listing (/catalogue/?page=N, with page 1 = /catalogue/), add <link rel="canonical"> pointing at each page's own clean URL, and publish a sitemap.xml listing the catalogue and product pages, referenced from robots.txt.

findings.summary: The page lists products (name, description, availability) but exposes no structured data and no share-preview metadata, so search and AI agents cannot read the items or their stock state as products.
findings.evidence: flow-probe: jsonLd=0, ogTags=0. Visible content: 3 product articles with names, descriptions and 'In stock' / 'Ordered on request' states.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a JSON-LD ItemList of Product entries (name, description, sku, offers.availability = InStock / PreOrder, and offers.price + priceCurrency once prices are shown, see F3), plus og:title, og:description and og:type for share previews.

It renders one column in the ~240-310px sidebar slot and one column at 360px without breaking. The forms (block labels, width:100% fields) adapt in both the 483px and 260px containers. The grid's unfortunate placement is a page-layout issue (F4), not a component failing to adapt.

All 10 page Tab stops show a 3px solid accent outline (:focus-visible); the 11th stop is the body wrap. Quantity uses type=number for a numeric keypad, and there are no hover-only affordances.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The h1 'Parts catalogue' states the purpose, but the products are pushed into the narrow sidebar column while the search card takes the wide one. The cards carry no action, and the add-to-cart action sits detached in a sidebar form.

checkOutcomes.evidence: 0 scripts and 0 inline handlers, so there are no deprecated APIs, unload handlers (no BFCache blocker), paste blockers or permission prompts. The console shows no deprecation warnings, and no source maps or libraries are shipped.

checkOutcomes.method: Overlay census, script inventory, console exception scan
checkOutcomes.evidence: There are no overlays or menus that could be clipped (0 overlays) and no async dependencies or visibility logic (0 scripts). 0 runtime exceptions across all loads.

checkOutcomes.method: resilience primitive (manifest, service worker, real offline reload)
checkOutcomes.evidence: No manifest linked and no page-origin service worker observed in a 2s window. The offline reload rendered the page from HTTP cache (317 chars), not from a worker.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a server-rendered catalogue MPA (a browse-and-order website), not an app with a standalone use case. Shopping requires live stock and a server-side cart, so installability and an offline shell are not expected here. Its server-failure handling is judged under network-and-http-failure-states.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative 404/501 routes reached from the page's own links and forms + screenshot of the failure page

checkOutcomes.method: Render diff under ar-EG vs default; inventory of rendered dates/numbers/currency

checkOutcomes.reason: The page currently renders no locale-sensitive data to format. The missing prices that should be locale-formatted are a commercial-clarity defect, judged under safe-commercial-and-account-flows (F3), whose fix carries the Intl formatting advice.
